summary: Record supported a finding that defense counsel impliedly consented to the jury receiving written final instructions. Trial court's handling of jury notes and mistrial/coercion issues was proper. Affirmed.
Applying Taranovich balancing, the Court held defendant's constitutional speedy-trial claim on a DWAI traffic infraction did not establish a violation. Affirmed.
Denial of defendant's CPL 440.20 motion to vacate his own illegally lenient sentence was not reviewable because the ruling did not adversely affect him under CPL 470.15 (1). Affirmed.

OGA accusatory instrument was facially insufficient because it failed to allege the specific official function (execution of a search warrant) with adequate notice. Reversed and accusatory instrument dismissed.

Sentencing court lacked authority to rely on improperly unsealed CPL 160.50 records from a favorably terminated case. Sentence vacated and matter remitted for resentencing without consideration of sealed materials.
Case summary and PSI constituted reliable hearsay sufficient to support SORA violence points under risk factor 1. Level-two adjudication affirmed.

Admission of DNA-profile testimony violated confrontation rights under John/Austin because the witness lacked the required role in profile generation or independent raw-data analysis. Error was not harmless; new trials ordered.

For SORA risk factor 9, defendant's New Jersey lewdness conviction was properly treated as tantamount to New York endangering the welfare of a child, supporting 30 points and a level-two designation. Affirmed.
Challenges to admission of out-of-court disclosure testimony and to lack of a limiting instruction were unpreserved; ineffective-assistance claim failed on this direct record. Affirmed.
In the Williams companion case, trial court should have held a Frye hearing before admitting LCN/FST evidence. Error was harmless given other proof, so conviction stood.
Same rule as Williams: denial of a Frye hearing on LCN/FST evidence was legal error, but harmless on this record. Affirmed.

Peque deportation-warning claim was unpreserved because defendant received a pre-plea immigration-consequences notice giving a reasonable opportunity to object. CPL 440 ineffective-assistance claim was properly denied without hearing. Affirmed.

Official-misconduct information was jurisdictionally sufficient, including allegations supporting unauthorized act, knowledge, and intent-to-benefit/deprive elements. Nonjurisdictional claims were forfeited by plea. Affirmed.

On direct appeal, record was insufficient to prove ineffective assistance from counsel's failure to challenge a juror; claim depended on matters dehors the record and belongs in CPL 440.10 proceedings. Affirmed.

CPL 710.70 (2) permits appellate review of a suppression ruling even where the guilty plea is to a different count within the same accusatory instrument and the suppressed evidence related to a satisfied count. Reversed and remitted to Appellate Division for suppression merits.
Appellate Division erred by affirming on an exigency ground not decided adversely to defendant by the suppression court, contrary to CPL 470.15 limits. Reversed and remitted for further proceedings.
Court of Appeals affirmed for the reasons stated in the Appellate Division memorandum.

People v Williams did not control because the federal marine interdiction agent was not a CPL peace officer; suppression based on Williams was error. Order reversed, suppression denied, and case remitted.
Trial court improperly replaced a sworn juror without the reasonably thorough CPL 270.35 (2) inquiry and record findings of unavailability. Reversed and new trial ordered.
Evidence and trial rulings, including treatment of third-party-guilt issues, grand-jury arguments, and evidentiary decisions, did not warrant reversal. Affirmed.
Traffic stop lacked objective probable cause or reasonable suspicion under the Vehicle and Traffic Law. Suppression granted and indictment dismissed.

CPL displaced Easton and does not permit factual amendment of informations/misdemeanor complaints to cure date defects; proper remedy was a superseding sworn instrument. Conviction reversed and accusatory instrument dismissed.
After a juror objected to repeated use of a racial slur, trial court acted within discretion by giving curative instructions and not conducting a separate Buford inquiry. Affirmed.

Court held no constitutional right to probable-cause discovery/adversarial hearing before buccal-swab warrant where notice and opportunity to be heard were provided; suppression ruling for defendant was erroneous. YouTube video was sufficiently authenticated. Appellate Division reversed and case remitted.

Suppression was improper because stopping a vehicle for a nonfunctioning center brake light was lawful at least as an objectively reasonable interpretation/mistake of law under governing Fourth Amendment standards. Reversed, suppression denied, and case remitted.

People failed to prove lawful basis for stop triggered by an MDT "similarity hit" because they did not establish the content/sufficiency of that information. Suppression granted and indictment dismissed.
Motion court abused discretion by denying CPL 330.30 (2) motion without the hearing required by CPL 330.40 and Maragh. Reversed and remitted for hearing.

Correction Law 73 (10) allows DOCCS to use an RTF as temporary residence for persons on community supervision beyond Penal Law 70.45 (3)'s initial six-month PRS-transfer period while SARA-compliant housing is unavailable. Affirmed.

As applied in these cases, temporary confinement of SARA-restricted level-three offenders pending compliant housing did not violate substantive due process or the Eighth Amendment. Orders modified to declaratory judgments and otherwise affirmed.

SARA's mandatory school-grounds condition in Executive Law 259-c (14) applies only to level-three offenders who are serving a sentence for an enumerated offense, not all level-three offenders. Affirmed.

Attempted murder convictions were unsupported because defendant's conduct amounted to planning/solicitation without acts dangerously near completion under New York attempt doctrine. Appellate Division affirmance of vacatur upheld.
Grand-jury evidence of intoxicated 119-mph flight with passengers and crash was legally sufficient for depraved-indifference assault charges. Affirmed.

Across ten cases, appeal waivers were invalid under Thomas because colloquies/forms mischaracterized waivers as absolute and failed to preserve surviving rights. Reversed and remitted for Appellate Division review of unresolved issues.

There was a reasonable view of evidence supporting a voluntary-possession instruction on the weapon count; refusing that charge was reversible error. New trial ordered on third-degree weapon possession count.

Defendant was not entitled to temporary-and-lawful-possession charge because initial possession was not legally excused under the evidence; justification for use does not excuse unlawful possession. Affirmed.

Appeal was not moot despite deportation, and Appellate Division did not abuse discretion by sustaining an upward SORA departure based on revenge-motive rape not adequately captured by guidelines. Affirmed.
Appeal dismissed as moot.

Under Lang, omission of non-elemental time information from indictment-waiver form is forfeited by guilty plea if not raised below; Appellate Division's dismissal of SCI was error. Reversed and remitted for unresolved issues.
